title: Uniform amplitude of proper direct image on classical finite-coefficient complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and $f:X\to Y$ a proper morphism of schemes. Suppose $e\in\mathbf N$ bounds the Krull dimension of every fibre after every base change [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-pc-base-change] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For $T=X,Y$ let $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},A_T)$ and $D_T=D(\mathcal A_T)$ be the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories and their unbounded derived categories, in a common universe in which the sites and all indexing families under consideration are small [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $G=Rf_{\mathrm{pro\acute et},*}$ for total K-injective direct image and use the classical-cohomology predicate of [sk-def-pe-classical-definition].
Then $G$ is triangulated, commutes with integer shifts, and preserves countable products with their canonical projections. For every integer $a$ and every $L\in D_X$, $L\in D_X^{\ge a}$ implies $G L\in D_Y^{\ge a}$. For every integer $b$ and every classical-cohomology $L\in D_X$, $L\in D_X^{\le b}$ implies $G L\in D_Y^{\le b+2e}$, even when $L$ is unbounded below. On the small étale sites with constant $A$ coefficients, $R^qf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}F=0$ for every $A$-module sheaf $F$ and $q>2e$, with higher direct images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The degree inequalities refer to the standard t-structures [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]. No quasi-compactness of $Y$ or bound on the cohomological dimension of a ground field is required. Moreover, the total étale direct image $E=Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}:D(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)\to D(Y_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)$ preserves every small ambient coproduct, with the canonical comparison whose components are $E$ of the coprojections [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

proof.text: The universe hypothesis makes the two ringed sites small. Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to their constant commutative ring sheaves: the module categories are Grothendieck abelian and have functorial K-injective resolutions. For these coefficients, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives the exact inverse image $f^*$, its module direct-image right adjoint $f_*$, and the total derived adjunction $D(f^*)\dashv G$. The additive direct image is left exact (kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise and $(f_*M)(V)=M(X\times_YV)$). Thus [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] applies and proves that $G$ carries distinguished triangles to distinguished triangles and commutes with integer shifts. Since $A$ is finite and discrete, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] identify the coefficient ring $A_T$ of the statement with the sheafified constant ring, i.e. with $\nu_T^*A_{T,\mathrm{\acute et}}$ as in [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]; so the constant-coefficient classical and comparison statements used in steps 5 and 6 apply to $\mathcal A_T$.

source.place: Setup for Transfer: total derived module direct image

proof.text:
Products of module sheaves exist: take the product of sections with componentwise scalar multiplication and restriction; a matching family glues uniquely in each component, so this presheaf is a sheaf, with the product universal property [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Choose K-injective representatives for a countable family. Their termwise product represents its derived product by [lem-pc-ringed-space-product-kinjective]; hence products exist in both derived categories. The adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] gives, for every $M\in D_Y$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,G\prod_iL_i)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(D(f^*)M,\prod_iL_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(D(f^*)M,L_i)\cong\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(M,GL_i).$$
These bijections are induced by $G$ of the product projections, so they are exactly the universal property that $G$ preserves the product, including its canonical projections.

source.place: Transfer: product preservation of total direct image

proof.text: If $L\in D_X^{\ge a}$, then $L$ belongs to the bounded-below subcategory, regardless of any upper bound. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] to the left exact additive $f_*$ between the Grothendieck categories obtained in step 1. Its bounded-below derived image has no cohomology below $a$. The comparison [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] identifies that image, after inclusion in the unbounded category, with $GL$. Therefore $GL\in D_Y^{\ge a}$.

Choose a positive integer $n$ with $n1_A=0$: among the finitely many multiples of $1_A$, two coincide, and their positive index difference works. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf of every étale $A$-module sheaf $F$ is killed by $n$. The identity base change in the assumed dimension bound supplies the fibre bound $e$ for $f$ itself. Apply [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] to this torsion abelian sheaf. It gives $R^qf_*U(F)=0$ for $q>2e$. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of the module $R^qf_*F$ with the same abelian derived cohomology. A module sheaf with zero underlying abelian sheaf is zero, so $R^qf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}F=0$ for $q>2e$. This argument uses neither quasi-compactness of $Y$ nor invertibility of $n$.

Properness gives finite type and separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Finite type includes quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. If $H$ is a classical pro-étale $A$-module sheaf, [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] writes $H\cong
u_X^*F$ for an étale $A$-module sheaf $F$, with $
u_T^*$ exact. Apply the bounded-below comparison [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] to $F[0]$; use [src-right-derived-functor-plus-compatibility] to interpret it for the total direct image. Then
$$G(H[0])\cong
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}(F[0]).$$
The sheaf-case derived identification [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] identifies the $q$-th cohomology on the right before pullback with $R^qf_{\mathrm{\acute et},*}F$. Step 4 kills it for $q>2e$; exactness of $
u_Y^*$ commutes with kernels, images and cokernels, so also with cohomology. Hence $G(H[0])\in D_Y^{\le2e}$.

source.place: Transfer: bounded-below étale/pro-étale comparison and heart bound

proof.text: Let $P$ be the class of classical $A$-module sheaves. It is replete by its definition as an essential image, and contains zero since $\nu_X^*0=0$ [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Step 5 supplies the heart bound $2e$, and step 1 supplies triangulatedness and shift commutation. Apply [lem-sfb-bounded-heart-amplitude-devissage] with this $P$ and $d=2e$. It follows that for every bounded classical-cohomology $K\in D_X^{\le b}$, one has $GK\in D_Y^{\le b+2e}$.

source.place: Transfer: finite Postnikov dévissage of the heart bound

proof.text: Now let $L\in D_X^{\le b}$ have classical cohomology, with no lower bound, and fix $m>b+2e$. Put $N=\min(b,m-2e-2)$. Then $N<m-2e-1$, and $K=\tau_{\ge N}L$ has cohomology in $[N,b]$, still classical: retained cohomology is unchanged and discarded cohomology is zero [def-kun-truncations]. Step 6 gives $\mathcal H^mGK=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-proper-classical-truncation] with $S=Y$ and the identity base change, identifying $X\times_YY$ with $X$ by its canonical projection. Its hypotheses are exactly the given properness, finite ring, uniform base-change fibre bound and classical cohomology, and its inequality is the chosen inequality on $N$. It identifies $\mathcal H^mGL$ with $\mathcal H^mGK=0$. Since this holds for every $m>b+2e$, the required sharp upper bound follows for the unbounded-below $L$.

source.place: Étale statements: output cohomology depends only on a bounded-below truncation; Transfer

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-exc-direct-image-coproducts] to the small étale sites, $u=f$ and $c=2e$. Step 5 has checked that $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and step 4 gives the vanishing for every étale $A$-module sheaf required by that criterion. It therefore gives the assertion for every small family of unbounded complexes, including the empty family. Its comparison is explicitly the map from the coproduct of the images to the image of the coproduct induced by applying $E$ to each coprojection, so it gives the specified canonical comparison, not just an abstract isomorphism. All families are small in the common universe fixed in the statement.
